g.text: You cannot replay commands. You can only replay events.
That single fact decides what has to be durable - and it is why all the durability effort lands on one append-only structure.
Command versus event - conflating them is the common mistake
past tense CANNOT fail - it happened
durable? YES - the source of truth
against whatever state exists now, and might call a fraud
API that answers differently. That does not reconstruct
history - it RE-DECIDES it. Replaying Debited(A, 10)
So ONLY the event log needs to be reliable.
Commands can be lost. State and snapshots can be corrupted and regenerated.
The discipline that makes replay work
if now() - account.last_active > 90 days: dormant = true
# RIGHT - the decision was made ONCE, and recorded
handle(command): # runs once; may be non-deterministic
Forbidden inside apply(): reading the clock, randomness, external I/O, iterating
unordered collections. A single now() in apply() silently breaks reproducibility -
and you will not discover it until an audit produces the wrong number months later.
State is a conclusion, not a record
a FOLD over history, not a stored value
Facts do not change, so history cannot be rewritten. Conclusions are recomputable, so a bug in the folding logic is fixable
RETROACTIVELY - fix the code and replay. Under a balance-storing schema, a bug that produced a wrong balance is permanent,
Each projection is an independent FOLD of the same events into whatever shape its queries want.
read models scale independently of the write path
a projection bug is fixable retroactively: fix, drop, replay
NEW read models can be built for data that PREDATES them - a monthly-statement feature
invented today works for the last three years. Commercially this is often worth more
the read side is fully EXPENDABLE: if projections fail, transfers keep working
The cost is a real user-facing problem: a user completes a transfer, refreshes, and sees their OLD balance.
Handled by exposing as_of_sequence, and by reading the write path directly for the one account they just touched.
